items.title: Dell PowerEdge R760 Installation and Service Manual
items.what_a_tech_uses_it_for: Walks a technician through opening the R760 chassis and swapping memory, drives, PSUs, fans, and expansion cards without guessing at screw locations.
items.notes: Covers the PowerEdge R760, a 2U dual-socket 4th/5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable server. WebFetch confirmed the page renders with a full table of contents.

items.title: PowerEdge: Rack Rail Types for Installation, Static Rails vs. Sliding Rails
items.what_a_tech_uses_it_for: Tells a technician which rail kit is in the box, static or sliding, and points to the matching PDF with the actual mounting steps.
key_procedures_inside: identifying static vs sliding rail kits
rail sizing and rack compatibility lookup
link to sliding rail installation PDF
link to static rail installation PDF
items.notes: The direct dl.dell.com sliding-rail installation PDF this page links to returned a 403 to automated fetch even after one retry, so this KB hub page is listed instead since it fetched cleanly and links onward to the same content.

items.title: Integrated Dell Remote Access Controller 9 (iDRAC9) User's Guide
items.what_a_tech_uses_it_for: Explains how to reach a PowerEdge server's out-of-band console, mount virtual media, read health and sensor status, and push firmware updates over iDRAC without needing the OS up.
key_procedures_inside: logging in and setting up network access
items.notes: This is the version 4.x guide; the same structure applies across the iDRAC9 firmware branches used on current PowerEdge rack servers.

items.vendor: Intel (IPMI consortium: Intel, HP, Dell, NEC)
items.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification, Second Generation, v2.0 (rev 1.1)
items.what_a_tech_uses_it_for: The reference for what IPMI sensor readings, event log entries, and chassis power-control commands actually mean on any BMC that predates or sits alongside Redfish.
items.notes: This is the long-standing canonical Intel-hosted URL for the v2.0 rev 1.1 spec used industry-wide (Dell, HPE, and Supermicro BMCs all implement it). WebFetch hit its 10MB size cap on the PDF itself. DMTF's own Redfish specification (DSP0266) was tried instead first for this slot, but dmtf.org returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every URL tried (the standards index page, the document landing page, and the direct PDF), so it was dropped per the fetch-failure rule; this IPMI spec covers the 'generic IPMI or Redfish reference' requirement instead.
